claims.text: A nanostructured dual-phase microstructure enables lightweight high-entropy alloys to combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Minor additions of reactive elements such as Al or Ti can form coherent oxide nanoprecipitates in a high-entropy solid-solution matrix.
Controlled oxidation during solidification or subsequent heat treatment produces well-distributed oxide nanoprecipitates.
The oxide nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
The oxide nanoprecipitates enhance mechanical strength through load transfer.
The oxide-containing microstructure refines grain size, which improves strength.
Oxide nanoprecipitates act as nucleation sites for a continuous protective oxide layer during high-temperature exposure.
The engineered microstructure establishes a stable, self-healing passivating surface layer.
The protective surface layer improves corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
High configurational entropy maintains overall phase stability in the oxide-strengthened alloy.
A uniform nanoprecipitate dispersion is required for the proposed performance improvements.
Excessive elemental segregation leads to coarse intermetallic phases and causes the proposed performance benefit to cease.
Reactive-element additions above a critical limit form brittle intermetallic compounds rather than coherent oxides.
Coarsening or inhomogeneity of the oxide nanoprecipitates prevents the expected mechanical and environmental improvements.
Atypical impurities or extreme thermal cycling can disrupt the protective oxide-scale mechanism.
The modified alloy will have greater yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have greater tensile strength with comparable or modestly reduced ductility relative to the baseline.
The modified alloy will exhibit lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
The modified alloy will exhibit a lower high-temperature oxidation rate and lower isothermal mass gain than the baseline.
Prior observations in oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloys and some high-entropy systems support a beneficial role for fine oxide precipitates.

contradictions.description: The intervention assigns a controlled solidification treatment to the modified alloy, and the experiment contrasts baseline 'standard processing' with modified processing, while the conditions and experiment also state that processing and heat treatments are identical for both alloys. It is therefore unclear whether composition alone or both composition and processing differ.
